content:
Wen Jiabao, Jia Qinglin and others attended the conference

A ceremony commemorating the 100th anniversary of Jiang Zemin's birth was held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Monday morning (17th). Xi Jinping, General Secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, President of the State and Chairman of the Central Military Commission, and all incumbent members of the Politburo Standing Committee attended. Retired leaders including Wen Jiabao, Jia Qinglin, Zhang Dejiang, Yu Zhengsheng, Li Zhanshu, Wang Yang, Li Lanqing, Zeng Qinghong, Li Changchun, He Guoqiang, Liu Yunshan, Wang Qishan and Zhang Gaoli also attended the ceremony.

Hu Jintao was not seen; Li Ruihuan, Wu Guanzheng and Luo Gan were absent

However, Hu Jintao, who succeeded Jiang Zemin as General Secretary of the CPC Central Committee, President of the State and Chairman of the Central Military Commission, was not seen in the live broadcast by China Central Television. In addition, Li Ruihuan, Wu Guanzheng and Luo Gan, who had served as members of the Politburo Standing Committee during Jiang's era, were also absent from the ceremony.

「1989嚴重政治風波 江堅決執行黨中央決策」

In his keynote address at the ceremony, Xi Jinping reviewed how Jiang Zemin rose from Shanghai Party secretary to become the core of the CPC's third generation of central collective leadership, and specifically said: 「A serious political disturbance occurred in China in the spring and summer of 1989. Comrade Jiang Zemin resolutely upheld and implemented the correct decisions of the CPC Central Committee, effectively safeguarding stability in Shanghai.」

Xi also called for learning Jiang's 「unyielding political faith」, saying that in the face of major tests presented by changing international circumstances in the late 1980s and early 1990s and a serious political disturbance at home, Jiang remained unwavering in his commitment to economic development. He also emphasised the approaches of governing the country first by governing the Party and of exercising strict governance over the Party.

Xi also said that Jiang's 「farsighted strategic thinking」 should be learned, noting that under Jiang's leadership, Hong Kong and Macao achieved smooth returns, while the two sides across the Taiwan Strait reached the 「1992 Consensus」, which embodies the one-China principle.

Attention has focused on Beijing's decision to hold a large-scale commemoration of Jiang's centenary at this time, and on the political signals sent by Xi's speech.

Independent political scholar Chen Daoyin said that holding a major event to mark the centenary of a deceased leader is an institutional convention. Many important leaders in the past, including Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping, had major centenary commemorations held in their honour. As the core of the CPC's third generation of central collective leadership, it is consistent with established practice and protocol to hold a large-scale ceremony for Jiang's centenary.

Scholar: The reference to 1989 contains no new formulation

Regarding Xi's active mention of Jiang's political stance in 1989 while commemorating him, Chen said 1989 was an important turning point both in China's politics and in Jiang's political career. That year, Jiang had been a local leader nearing retirement but was appointed to a critical new post because he had 「chosen the right side」, and was transferred to Beijing to replace Zhao Ziyang, becoming the core of the CPC's third generation of central collective leadership. As a result, any review of his life must address the events of 1989.

Chen said Jiang's firm support for the decisions of the CPC Central Committee at the time echoes Xi's current political requirement of upholding the authority of the Central Committee and the core, making it all the more necessary to raise the matter again. He also believed that Xi's remarks concerning 1989 were all part of the established assessment of Jiang's legacy, without introducing any new formulation, and that outsiders should not overinterpret Xi's renewed reference to 1989.

Hu Jintao, the core of the CPC's fourth generation of central collective leadership, was absent from the large-scale commemoration of Jiang's centenary. Chen said retired leaders are not necessarily required to attend such events, but as Jiang's successor, Hu would ordinarily have been expected to attend a major event commemorating him. His absence could be due to factors such as not being in Beijing or feeling unwell. He pointed out that attention could be paid to whether Hu sent a floral tribute for former Premier Zhu Rongji's funeral on Tuesday (18th).

Chao Chien-min, former dean of the College of Social Sciences at Chinese Culture University in Taiwan, who specialises in China's political development and cross-strait relations, said Xi's speech that day provided a comprehensive review of Jiang's life. Several important milestones in Jiang's political career, including proposing the important thought of the 「Three Represents」, the two sides across the Taiwan Strait reaching the 「1992 Consensus」, and Jiang's resolute support for the decisions of the CPC Central Committee in 1989, are all unavoidable elements in any review of his legacy.

Chao said it was a normal approach for Xi to mention only that Jiang firmly stood on the side of the CPC Central Committee in 1989, without making further comments on the June 4 incident.

Chao also pointed out that Xi's emphasis on the centenary of Jiang's birth also had a personal dimension. He believed that the promotions Xi later received—from a leading official in Fujian to serving successively as the top official in the economically important provinces of Zhejiang and Shanghai—laid the foundation for his entry into the highest levels of leadership, and that Jiang had played an important and crucial role in that process.

He believed Xi's emphasis on commemorating Jiang showed, on the one hand, that Xi valued old ties and felt gratitude; on the other hand, by assessing Jiang and highlighting his efforts to promote strict governance of the Party and combat corruption, Xi could also demonstrate that the related policies inherited and continued the direction of work from the Jiang era. This represented the implementation of an existing consensus within the Party and could help clarify rumours circulating in public.

The importance of obeying the CPC Central Committee at moments of major right and wrong must be highlighted

However, veteran China political commentator Cai Shenkun held a different view. He described Xi's public mention of Jiang's stance during the 1989 「political disturbance」 as unusual, and said that while Jiang was alive—and even his family after his death—had wished to downplay, rather than emphasise, how he had risen to the centre of supreme power as a result of the June 4 incident.

Cai believed Xi's special emphasis on this point was intended to highlight the importance of obeying the CPC Central Committee and maintaining political loyalty at moments involving major questions of right and wrong.

Cai also noted that the CPC's 21st National Congress, commonly known as the 「20th?」, is expected to convene next autumn. Wait, if source says "21st National Congress", Chinese would be 中共二十一大, not "20th?". The translation should reflect 21st, not typo. He believed Xi's emphasis on Jiang's centenary and his praise of Jiang's choice to firmly support the CPC Central Committee served, on the one hand, to emphasise the political succession relationship between Xi and Jiang and strengthen the legitimacy of political continuity; on the other hand, commemorating Jiang could also reiterate to Party members the importance of obeying the central leadership and maintaining political loyalty.
